+# Flow 03 — Registration and email verification
+
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda)

+Mode: specification only; no product implementation, email delivery, Google authentication, backend security, browser run, or verification is authorized or claimed

+## 1. Authority and scope
+
+This flow follows [the shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md), then the latest owner answers, then unchanged behavior in [SPEC-001](../specifications/SPEC-001_dubbed_mvp.md) and [BR-001](../business-requirements/BR-001_custom_video_dubbing.md).

+
+- creation of a pending email/password registration;
+- visible instructions and recovery while email verification is pending;
+- resolution of an email-verification proof;
+- completion of registration only after authoritative verification succeeds;
+- the handoff to Flow 05 when a verified identity needs explicit ownership-verified linking;
+- presentation of the authoritative one-time welcome-credit result after eligible completion;
+- Google authentication as an alternative entry action, with its result handed to the shared authentication flow.
+
+It does not own sign-in, password reset, account linking, account settings, account deletion, or the final signed-in destination contracts. Those belong to Flows 02, 04, 05, and 15.
+
+## 2. Confirmed product contract
+
+- Email/password registration cannot complete until the email address is verified.
+- Google authentication is available as an alternative to email/password registration.
+- A matching Google and email/password address is not proof of common ownership.
+- A match may produce only an authoritative `link_required` continuation to Flow 05; it must not auto-merge, sign in, move data, or issue a second grant.
+- The identity service is authoritative for pending-registration state, proof validity, verified status, account status, session eligibility, and linking eligibility.
+- An eligible verified account receives exactly 120 welcome credits once.
+- Welcome credits do not expire.
+- Reload, callback replay, repeated completion, Google relinking, and account-method linking must not duplicate the grant.
+- The browser displays authoritative account and grant results; it never computes or issues the grant.
+- English and Russian are supported on desktop and phone.
+- The visual direction is light, flat, white/light-gray, readable, and free of gradients or decorative effects.
+- Guest authentication screens use compact top navigation and no permanent sidebar.
+
+## 3. Purpose, entry, and exit
+
+### 3.1 Purpose
+
+The screen answers one question first: **What must I do to create and verify my account?**
+
+The most frequent action is the current primary action: create the pending registration, submit the selected proof form, or continue after successful verification. Only one of these is primary at a time.
+
+### 3.2 Entry
+
+Supported entry contexts are:
+
+1. A guest chooses registration from Flow 01 or Flow 02.
+2. A guest reaches the registration route with a safe return intent supplied by another flow.
+3. A person opens an email-delivered verification entry on the same or another device.
+4. A person reloads or revisits a still-valid pending-registration screen.
+5. An identity service response returns a verification or registration result that must be reconciled.
+
+A return intent is only navigation context. It cannot bypass verification, linking, account status, or session checks.
+
+### 3.3 Exit
+
+Possible exits are:
+
+- verified registration success to the destination and session behavior selected in `OPEN-F03-03`;
+- successful Google authentication to Flow 02's shared authenticated continuation;
+- `link_required` to Flow 05 with an opaque, server-owned linking intent;
+- existing-account sign-in to Flow 02;
+- password recovery to Flow 04;
+- cancellation/back to the safe referring public route;
+- a terminal blocked state when the service reports that registration cannot continue.
+
+No exit may claim a signed-in session, verified email, linked method, or granted credits before the responsible service confirms it.
+
+## 4. Information architecture and visual anatomy
+
+### 4.1 Shared frame
+
+- A compact top bar carries product identity, locale access, and the relevant sign-in/register alternative.
+- There is no sidebar.
+- The main region has one `h1`, one plain supporting sentence, the active form or status, and only the recovery actions needed for that state.
+- The interface uses flat light surfaces, readable full-ink text, quiet borders on real form controls, and no gradients, glass, glow, or decorative illustration.
+- Exact colors, fonts, radii, widths, spacing, and breakpoints remain shared OPEN design decisions.
+
+### 4.2 Desktop composition
+
+- The form is a focused, bounded reading column inside the shared top-navigation shell.
+- The column must not be presented as a floating marketing card with a decorative shadow.
+- Product identity and locale stay available without competing with the form.
+- Errors appear with the field or operation they explain; a service outage may use one compact in-flow status region.

+
+- The same reading order is preserved in one column with 16–20 px outer margins as a design target, subject to the shared token decision.
+- Every interactive target is at least 44 CSS px in both dimensions.
+- The primary action remains visible after the relevant fields without relying on a fixed overlay.
+- The keyboard must not cover the focused field, validation message, or submit result.
+- Long email addresses wrap or truncate without horizontal page scrolling while retaining an accessible full value.

+### 4.4 Form rules
+
+- Every field has a persistent visible label; placeholder text never substitutes for a label.
+- Password fields support paste and password managers.
+- Any show/hide-password control has an accessible name and does not change the field value.
+- Submit remains available for ordinary client-side mistakes so attempted submission can reveal actionable validation; only an active duplicate request may temporarily disable it.

+### 5.1 Create account

+Required content:
+
+- title and short explanation;
+- **Continue with Google** / **Продолжить с Google**;
+- a clear separator expressed in words, not decoration alone;
+- labeled email and password fields;
+- password requirements derived only from the selected policy;
+- **Create account** / **Создать аккаунт**;
+- **Sign in** / **Войти** link for an existing account;
+- locale control from the shared shell.
+
+The Google action starts the shared provider-authentication boundary. This specification does not claim a real provider, popup, redirect, consent screen, or callback implementation.
+
+### 5.2 Submission pending
+
+- The submitted action shows an in-place busy state and prevents duplicate starts.
+- Field values remain visible except that the password is never echoed outside its protected input.
+- A retry after an unknown result must reconcile the original attempt before creating another pending registration.
+- Reload during an unknown result resolves from the service; the UI must not infer failure from a timeout.
+
+### 5.3 Verification pending
+
+The screen shows:
+
+- **Check your email** / **Проверьте почту**;
+- the destination address in the display treatment selected in `OPEN-F03-10`;
+- instructions matching the verification method selected in `OPEN-F03-01`;
+- resend availability and feedback governed by `OPEN-F03-07`;
+- a route to correct a mistyped email governed by `OPEN-F03-08`;
+- **Sign in** for a person who already completed registration elsewhere;
+- a non-secret pending-state reference suitable for reload reconciliation.
+
+It must not say that an email was delivered when a mock or service has only accepted the request.
+
+### 5.4 Verification proof resolution
+
+The selected method is OPEN:
+
+- **Link:** an email entry supplies an opaque proof to the resolver and shows a short resolving state.
+- **Code:** the screen supplies a labeled code field, paste support, submit action, and code-specific validation.
+- **Both:** would require both paths and a clear switch/recovery rule; it is not included unless selected.
+
+Proof outcomes are distinct service facts:
+
+- valid and registration completed;
+- valid but explicit account linking required;
+- malformed or invalid proof;
+- expired proof;
+- already-used proof;
+- proof does not belong to the active pending registration;
+- pending registration no longer exists or cannot continue;
+- temporarily unavailable or result unknown.
+
+Exact copy and recovery differences among invalid, expired, used, and mismatched proofs remain `OPEN-F03-09`. The UI must never convert any of them to success locally.
+
+### 5.5 Verified success
+
+Success shows only facts returned by authoritative services:
+
+- email verification and registration completion;
+- session state, if the selected contract creates one;
+- authoritative welcome-credit balance or grant result, when available;
+- the next action selected in `OPEN-F03-03`.
+
+The page may say **120 welcome credits added** only when the returned account state proves this registration caused the eligible grant. If the grant already existed, display the current authoritative balance or a neutral completion message without implying a second grant.
+
+### 5.6 Google alternative outcomes
+
+- Provider success continues through Flow 02's session/destination contract.
+- Provider cancellation returns to the unchanged registration screen without an account-success claim.
+- Provider denial or failure gives a concise retry and keeps email/password registration available.
+- `link_required` hands off to Flow 05; Flow 03 does not explain or perform the merge itself.
+- Unknown callback status reconciles through the identity service before retry.
+
+## 6. Main and alternate transitions
+
+### 6.1 Email/password happy path
+
+1. Enter email and password.
+2. Submit **Create account**.
+3. Service returns a pending registration and verification-delivery status.
+4. Show verification-pending instructions.
+5. Resolve the selected verification proof.
+6. Service atomically reports completed registration or `link_required`.
+7. On completion, read authoritative account, session, and grant state.
+8. Continue according to the selected post-verification behavior.
+
+### 6.2 Resend
+
+1. Request resend from the active pending registration.
+2. Show a busy state without clearing the pending context.
+3. Render an accepted, throttled, unavailable, or unknown result.
+4. Do not reset proof lifetime, replace prior proofs, or promise delivery unless the selected service policy says so.
+
+TTL, cooldown, rate limit, response privacy, and whether older proofs remain valid are OPEN.
+
+### 6.3 Email typo correction
+
+The interface must provide a recoverable route for a mistyped address, but the contract is OPEN on whether it edits the pending registration or restarts one. It must not carry a password into a new identity request without an explicitly selected safe contract.
+
+### 6.4 Reload and cross-device entry
+
+- Reload reconciles the pending registration from an opaque reference; local state is never sufficient proof.
+- An email proof opened on another device can be resolved without assuming access to the originating browser state.
+- Whether a successful cross-device verification also creates a session there is part of `OPEN-F03-03`.
+- A used proof is idempotent only to the extent the service can safely return the already-completed result; it must not repeat side effects.
+
+## 7. Logical service boundary
+
+Names below describe frontend responsibilities, not implemented APIs.
+
+| Logical operation | Inputs | Required result categories |
+|---|---|---|
+| Start registration | normalized-for-transport email input, password secret, locale, safe return intent | pending reference, delivery request status, field conflict, rate limit, unavailable, unknown |
+| Read pending registration | opaque pending reference | pending, verified/completed, link required, expired/closed, unavailable |
+| Resend verification | opaque pending reference | accepted, throttled with service guidance, closed, unavailable, unknown |
+| Change registration email | opaque pending reference plus newly entered address and any required fresh proof | updated/replaced pending state or actionable rejection |
+| Resolve verification proof | opaque proof and any service-required pending context | completed, link required, invalid, expired, used, mismatched, unavailable, unknown |
+| Read auth completion | opaque completion reference | session/account facts, safe destination, link required, blocked account |
+| Read credit state | canonical account identity/session | authoritative balance and exactly-once welcome-grant status |
+| Start Google authentication | locale and safe return intent | provider handoff, cancellation, denial, success, link required, unknown |
+
+The centralized frontend services boundary may have an interchangeable mock. A mock must mark email delivery, provider authentication, proof validation, session creation, and grant issuance as simulation; it is not evidence that any production service exists or is secure.
+
+## 8. Persistence, privacy, and security-visible behavior
+
+- Passwords are never placed in URLs, analytics, logs, local persistence, error copy, or mock fixtures.
+- Verification secrets are treated as secrets even when delivered in a URL.
+- Browser history and visible copy must avoid exposing proof material after resolution where the platform allows safe cleanup.
+- Pending-registration persistence stores only the opaque reference and non-secret presentation state allowed by the selected policy.
+- Email addresses are shown only where needed for confirmation and correction; masking behavior remains OPEN.
+- Responses for existing, deleted, blocked, or already-registered addresses must follow the selected privacy policy; enumeration behavior is not invented here.
+- Client timers may display service-provided resend/expiry guidance but cannot decide validity.
+- Completion, linking eligibility, grant issuance, and session creation require authoritative idempotent service handling.
+- No frontend specification can claim transport security, token entropy, password hashing, abuse prevention, or provider authenticity without backend evidence.
+
+## 9. Accessible interaction
+
+- Reading and tab order follow the visible order: shell, title, provider action, email/password form, secondary links, then state-specific recovery.
+- Every field exposes programmatic label, purpose, error association, and valid autocomplete metadata.
+- Error focus moves to the first invalid field for field failures and to the status summary for operation failures.
+- Status changes use a polite live region; blocking failures use an assertive announcement only when immediate action is required.
+- Keyboard users can operate password visibility, submit, resend, email correction, locale selection, and all recovery actions.
+- Focus remains visible against every light surface and returns to the initiating control after a dismissed transient UI.
+- Proof inputs, if selected, accept paste and do not force one-character boxes.
+- Copy does not rely on color, icons, or elapsed animation to communicate status.
+- Motion is limited to user-triggered feedback and respects reduced-motion preferences.
+
+## 10. Core English/Russian copy
+
+| Purpose | English | Russian |
+|---|---|---|
+| Registration title | Create your account | Создайте аккаунт |
+| Google action | Continue with Google | Продолжить с Google |

+| Expired proof | This verification has expired. | Срок действия подтверждения истёк. |
+| Retry | Try again | Повторить |

+

+

+- [ ] **F03-AC02 — Alternative method:** Google authentication is available and its success, cancellation, denial, unknown, and `link_required` results have explicit paths without being simulated as production.

+- [ ] **F03-AC06 — Password form:** labels, paste, password-manager support, show/hide accessibility, confirmation behavior, and visible requirements match the selected policy. **BLOCKED by `OPEN-F03-02` and `OPEN-F03-05`.**
+- [ ] **F03-AC07 — Post-success behavior:** session creation, destination, return-intent handling, and cross-device behavior match the selected contract. **BLOCKED by `OPEN-F03-03`.**
+- [ ] **F03-AC08 — Pending recovery:** reload and email-entry reconciliation cover pending, completed, link-required, invalid, expired, used, mismatched, closed, unavailable, and unknown states without local success inference.
+- [ ] **F03-AC09 — Resend:** cooldown, limits, privacy, expiry interaction, duplicate request behavior, and visible feedback match selected policy. **BLOCKED by `OPEN-F03-06` and `OPEN-F03-07`.**
+- [ ] **F03-AC10 — Email correction:** a mistyped address has a safe recovery path with explicit secret re-entry and pending-state treatment. **BLOCKED by `OPEN-F03-08`.**
+- [ ] **F03-AC11 — Honest services:** mock email, Google, proof, session, and credit behavior is labeled simulation; production capability is claimed only from integrated evidence.
+- [ ] **F03-AC12 — Responsive access:** English and Russian layouts work at agreed desktop and phone widths, with 44 px touch targets, no page-level horizontal scrolling, visible focus, and complete keyboard operation.
+- [ ] **F03-AC13 — Visual contract:** the flow uses the compact top-navigation shell, no sidebar, light white/gray flat surfaces, quiet real-control borders, and no gradients or decorative effects.
+- [ ] **F03-AC14 — Secret handling:** passwords and verification proof material do not enter URLs, logs, analytics, persisted UI state, copy, or fixtures beyond the minimum transport boundary.
+

+
+The following is a future evidence plan, not a report of passing behavior:
+
+- Component interaction checks for labels, validation association, password visibility, paste, submit locking, resend, email correction, focus movement, and live-region announcements.
+- Service-contract checks for every result category in Section 7, including unknown-result reconciliation.
+- State-machine checks for reload before delivery, while pending, after verification, after proof expiry, after proof use, and during `link_required` handoff.

+- Google alternative scenarios for cancellation, denial, callback replay, provider outage, unknown result, and explicit linking.
+- Localization checks with realistic long English and Russian copy and long email addresses.
+- Keyboard-only and screen-reader checks on desktop and phone-sized layouts.
+- Rendered visual checks at the eventual shared desktop, tablet, and 390 px phone widths after tokens and geometry are approved.
+- Integrated email/provider/backend checks only when real services exist; mocked checks must remain labeled simulation.
+

+
+## 13. Dependencies and handoffs
+
+| Dependency | Responsibility |
+|---|---|
+| Shared contract / Flow 01 | Product identity, compact top navigation, locale entry, responsive shell, and eventual visual tokens |
+| Flow 02 — Sign in | Existing-account entry, Google/session continuation, return intent, expired-session handling, and final authenticated destination |
+| Flow 04 — Password reset | Recovery for an existing email/password identity; never completes this pending registration |
+| Flow 05 — Account linking | Explicit ownership proofs and linking of Google with a verified email/password method |
+| Flow 12 — Credits | Authoritative balance and exactly-once grant presentation after completion |
+| Flow 15 — Account | Verified-email/account status presentation and later method-management entry points |
+| Identity/email/provider services | Pending identity, delivery, proof validity, account status, provider proof, session, abuse controls, and idempotency |
+
+Flow 03 supplies a verified completion result, a safe authentication continuation, or an opaque `link_required` intent. It does not supply password-reset proof, linking proof, account settings, or locally asserted credit state.
+
+## 14. OPEN owner decisions
+
+1. `OPEN-F03-01` — Verification method: email link, email code, or both.
+2. `OPEN-F03-02` — User-visible password policy, including minimum length and any composition rules.
+3. `OPEN-F03-03` — After successful verification: whether a session is created, whether a success interstitial appears, destination, return-intent precedence, and cross-device behavior.
+4. `OPEN-F03-04` — Pending-registration retention and abandonment behavior before verification.
+5. `OPEN-F03-05` — Whether password confirmation is required and how mismatch is shown.
+6. `OPEN-F03-06` — Verification-proof TTL and whether resend invalidates older proofs or changes expiry.
+7. `OPEN-F03-07` — Resend cooldown, attempt limit/window, service guidance, and privacy-preserving response behavior.
+8. `OPEN-F03-08` — Mistyped-email recovery: edit pending identity or restart, password re-entry, and handling of the old address/proofs.
+9. `OPEN-F03-09` — Distinct copy and recovery actions for malformed, invalid, expired, used, mismatched, and closed proofs.
+10. `OPEN-F03-10` — Whether and how the destination email is masked on pending and error screens.
+11. `OPEN-F03-11` — Account-enumeration policy for existing, blocked, deleted, or already-registered addresses.
+12. `OPEN-F03-12` — Exact shared tokens, typography, control geometry, column width, and approved responsive breakpoints.
+
+No affected acceptance criterion is ready for implementation until its OPEN decisions are resolved and the resulting contract is reviewed.
